faqs.q: Why do bats roost in Franklin farmhouses and older homes?
faqs.a: Quiet attics in valley homes near cave-and-creek insect country are classic big brown bat roosts. Remember the county's cave bats are protected and never ours to disturb — house colonies are handled by exclusion only, under the Division's guidelines, and any listed species is a referral to WVDNR.

Franklin.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Franklin calls follow the ground the town sits on: south Branch Potomac River (along the town), Germany Valley karst to the west, forested ridges rising on both sides of the farm valley (Franklin is the Pendleton County seat). That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, striped skunks, woodchucks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

The pattern repeats yearly: raccoon and squirrel denning in spring, bats and digging animals through summer, and a hard rodent and squirrel push into heated homes each fall. Franklin is a small historic town of 1800s homes and brick blocks in the South Branch valley. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.

faqs.q: What is burrowing around Brandywine barns and gardens?
faqs.a: Woodchucks — the South Fork's farm edges are prime burrow ground. We remove the animals at the burrow, advise on backfilling, and check the fence lines where replacements arrive from.
